questions.question: What is "settler colonialism"?
options: Colonisers permanently occupy and build a society on indigenous land
Colonisers only extract resources and leave
questions.explanation: Settler colonialism is where colonisers permanently occupy indigenous land, as in the US, Canada, Australia and New Zealand.

questions.question: What does "self-determination" mean for indigenous peoples?
options: The right to freely determine their political status and development
The right to free healthcare only
questions.explanation: Self-determination is the right of indigenous peoples to freely determine their political status and pursue their development.

questions.question: Which 2007 UN document is the most important on indigenous rights?
options: UNDRIP (UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples)
questions.explanation: UNDRIP (2007) is the most important international document on indigenous rights, affirming self-determination and land rights.

questions.question: What is "intergenerational trauma"?
options: Psychological and social harm transmitted across generations
questions.explanation: Intergenerational trauma is harm transmitted across generations, e.g. from residential schools and forced removals.

questions.question: Which indigenous people in Norway have experienced similar patterns of assimilation?
questions.explanation: Norway's Sami people have experienced similar patterns of assimilation and continue to fight for their rights.
